name: REA — Reverse Engineer Anything via MCP
hook: 382.8k stars and growing fast — 234k on Oct 14, 330k on Oct 19, 382.8k today. REA is an MIT-licensed MCP server + CLI that hands any coding agent 50 reverse-engineering tools: native binaries via Hopper/Ghidra/IDA, Electron apps via static JS inspection, .NET assemblies, Android APKs, firmware, and packet captures. Analysis runs locally; no binary leaves your machine. One command registers the server and writes agent config across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI. Fastest-growing item in the claude-code topic by star velocity.

name: Ponytail — Laziness-First Code Skill
hook: 176k stars (+3.1k since Oct 22). Forces agents through a decision ladder before writing a line: does it already exist? Can stdlib do it? Can a single line solve it? Author benchmarks on 39 tasks / 5 runs in Opus 5.5 show −53% lines, −26% cost, −41% time. `/ponytail-review` hunts complexity instead of correctness; `/ponytail-audit` ranks what to delete repo-wide. Claude Code 2.1.290+ gets a live band showing cost, tokens, and code-reuse percentage per session.

name: Caveman — Token-Reduction Skill and Proxy
hook: 115k+ stars, Day 3 of trending. Cuts tokens three ways: terse agent replies (63 → 20 tokens on a React answer), compressed log/JSON/CSV output (measured 33.2% input-token reduction per session), and reusable script blocks (397 → 76 tokens on a test run). An Auto mode routes each request to the cheapest model and effort level, claiming 54% savings vs Opus at xhigh. Works in Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI.

name: Graphify — Codebase-to-Knowledge-Graph

install: uv tool install graphifyy && graphify install
